id: title:MattPua:cache timezone date parsing across charts

review.posthog_relevance: Reduces CPU and memory usage in frontend chart rendering by caching timezone parsing results, preventing redundant computation and unbounded memory growth when dashboards share repeated date labels.
review.reason: P1.F2.H2 implements a bounded cache with a size limit for timezone parsing. This demonstrates a substantive, bounded improvement in resource efficiency and reliability for the frontend rendering path, consistent with a tier 2 assessment. P1.F1.H1 is a test assertion and does not demonstrate the implementation behavior, so it is excluded. No unverified adoption or incident avoidance
review.uncertainty: The benefit relies on the assumption that repeated date strings occur frequently enough in PostHog dashboards to realize the CPU savings, and that the cache implementation does not introduce other performance overheads, neither of which is independently verified in this chunk.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains three hunks. P1.F1.H1 is a test assertion. P1.F2.H1 and P1.F2.H2 are implementation. P1.F2.H2 is the primary implementation hunk. P1.F1.H1 is not an implementation hunk and does not demonstrate the behavior of the implementation, so it is excluded from observations. P1.F2.H1 and P1.F2.H2 are treated as one group.

observations.behavior: Adds a cache and a size limit to the timezone parsing function. P1.F2.H2: P1.F2.H2 adds a Map and a limit constant, then checks the cache before parsing. P1.F2.H1: P1.F2.H1 adds the cache and limit declarations.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces CPU and memory usage when charts with many labels are rendered, especially if the same date strings appear repeatedly. PostHog dashboards often share labels across charts; caching avoids re-parsing identical date strings. The limit prevents unbounded memory growth if many unique date strings are cached.
